statement: Byrnes' proof loses effectivity at exactly one step: the converse direction of Lemma 4 ('Finally, suppose that k in Q(A). Since any A_{m,n} is finite, we can find an M and N such that...'), which extracts M and N from the bare finiteness of the set of positions with g-value k. That step is the sole source of T(A,k) and hence of W(A,k), and W(A,k) is the ONLY non-computable term in the final bound. The Lemma 9 pigeonhole is explicit: p_{A,k} <= 4^(|A|+k) p and N_{A,k} <= N + 4^(|A|+k) p.

statement: Zeilberger's exposition is a DIFFERENT proof of the 3-row case and contains no non-effective step. Its pigeonhole is over the explicitly counted state space S_a = (I_a; L_{a-1},...,L_{a-M}), giving N(r) + period(r) <= p_r (M_r+1)^(M_r) with M_r a bound on p-q below r and p_r = lcm{period(c) : c<r}. An effective Byrnes for 3-row Chomp therefore needs only (Z1) an explicit bound on max_q (f(q,r)-q), and (Z2) a bound on the lcm of the periods below r.

statement: NOVELTY: Hegarty-Larsson (INTEGERS 6 (2006) #A03) Theorem 3.3 gives only the ASYMPTOTIC DENSITY (L,l) of greedy difference permutations, with NO error term: the proof states the convergence rate is determined by M+,M-,S and "We omit any further details". Their Conjecture 5.1 (and 6.4) is EXACTLY the strip-bound statement we need: there exists c=c_{m,p} with pi_{m,p}(n) within c of floor(nL) or floor(nl). This is stated OPEN in their paper. So the strip bound |A029902(n)-a n|<=K is not in the literature; it is (morally) H&L Conjecture 5.1 specialised, and H&L machinery does NOT directly deliver an error term. Also: a=1+sqrt2/2 and b=1+sqrt2 satisfy 1/a+1/b=1 exactly (Beatty pair) and b=sqrt2*a exactly.

statement: SELF-SIMILARITY (exact form of the renormalization fixed point). For the stale rows A029902 and a=1+sqrt(2)/2, b=1+sqrt(2) (=sqrt(2)*a exactly, Beatty pair 1/a+1/b=1), the discrepancy D(x)=#{A029902<=x}-x/a satisfies D(x)+D(bx) in {-1,0,1} for every integer x with bx<=50000. Equivalently #{A029902<=x}+#{A029902<=bx}=2x+{-1,0,1}. This is the self-similarity the Friedman-Landsberg picture predicts, in exact (not merely asymptotic) form: the stale set is invariant under x->bx up to a discrepancy of magnitude <=1.

statement: NEGATIVE RESULT: the stale/live indicator word w(n)=[n is a stale constant A029901] over n=1..50000 is NOT Sturmian and NOT of low (linear) factor complexity. Factor complexity c(k)=#{distinct length-k factors} grows superlinearly: c(2)=4 (Sturmian would be 3), c(5)=22, c(10)=234, c(20)=7579, and reaches the maximal possible value min(2^k, N-k+1) by k~40. So any proof route requiring the word to be Sturmian/balanced/morphic-of-low-complexity is dead: A029901 has essentially maximal subword complexity while still having bounded discrepancy (C0016). This is the 'chaos' in Zeilberger's title: bounded discrepancy coexists with high complexity.

evidence: exact integer computation N(x)+N(floor(bx))-2x over x=1..20710 (bx<=50000): values {-1:4955, 0:14114, 1:1641}, nothing else. Iteration identity D(x)=e(x)-D(bx) verified symbolically; alternating-sum formal solution noted (needs the tail to vanish, i.e. D bounded at infinity, which is circular but pinpoints the structure).
statement: EXACT INTEGER FORM + ITERATION. With N(x)=#{A029902<=x}, the self-similarity is the exact integer relation N(x)+N(floor(b x)) = 2x + e(x), e(x) in {-1,0,1} (no floating point; x/a + bx/a = 2x exactly since 1/a+1/b=1... correction: x/a+bx/a = x(1+b)/a = 2x). Rewriting in D(x)=N(x)-x/a: D(x)+D(floor(bx))=e(x). Iterating the cocycle gives the formal solution D(x) = sum_{k>=0} (-1)^k e(floor(b^k x)) (plus a vanishing tail), so boundedness of D is EQUIVALENT to boundedness of these alternating base-b digit sums. This shows the self-similarity is a cocycle/substitution equation: it does NOT by itself force D bounded (adversarial e could make the alternating sum grow), so the mex structure must supply the self-consistency of e. The e-values are NOT arbitrary: e(x) in {-1,0,1} is determined by D, and the actual distribution is {0:14114, -1:4955, 1:1641} for x with bx<=50000.

evidence: counterexample verified symbolically: k=floor(log_b x), D(x)=(-1)^k k, then D(x)+D(b x)=(-1)^{k+1} in {-1,1} and D unbounded. So bounded e does not imply bounded D.
statement: NEGATIVE RESULT (kills Route A as stated): the cocycle D(x)+D(floor(bx)) in {-1,0,1} does NOT by itself force D bounded. Explicit counterexample: D(x)=(-1)^k * k with k=floor(log_b x) satisfies D(x)+D(bx) in {-1,1} for all x while D is unbounded. Therefore the mex structure of A029901/A029902 must supply the self-consistency of e(x)=N(x)+N(floor(bx))-2x; the self-similarity is a CONSEQUENCE of the structure, not a sufficient condition. Route A needs the additional constraint that e is itself generated by the greedy mex rule (D(x)-D(x-1) = [x in A902] - 1/a, and A902 is the mex-determined set).

statement: EXACT BLOCK-COUNT IDENTITY and BOUNDED-DIP STRUCTURE of the mex-generated diagonal. Let c_n=|(R_n \ D_{<n}) cap [1,d_n)| (non-diagonal row-n tops below the mex), fdip(n)=#{a>=n: d_a<d_n} (future dips), delta_n=#{a<n: d_a>=d_n} (past dips). Then EXACTLY (mex coverage + complementarity C0031): c_n = #{constants q_m < d_n} + fdip(n). Value: exact decomposition of the block count + a clean monotonicity target. Verified: at every dip event (71 to n=5000) the unique a with d_a>=d_n is ALWAYS a=n-1, and d_n = d_{n-1}-1 (single-step). So the dip is exactly 'row-(n-1) top d_{n-1}-1 is not carried into R_n, becomes the gap'. This explains single-step dips mechanistically and is consistent with delta_n<=1 (the dip affects only a=n-1). Exact: delta_n = 2n - |D_{<n} cap R_n| - d_n + 1 (from |D u R|=(d_n-1)+delta_n and |D u R|=2n-|D cap R|). So delta_n<=1 <=> |D cap R| >= 2n-d_n, and the overlap |D cap R|~(2-alpha)n IS the density (C0063) = the strip bound. Measured overlap-(2n-d_n)=1 (so delta_n=0 at non-dips). So proving delta_n<=1 requires the overlap density = the full strip bound. The dip MECHANISM (row-top drop-out) is genuine but explains only WHY dips are single-step, NOT the <=1 bound (which needs the density). Do NOT treat 'almost-increasing' as a tractable sub-lemma -- it is the hard problem.

statement: EXACT MEX-SANDWICH IDENTITY, rigorous conditional on one isolated game premise. Under premise (P): for every n, R_n={f(n,b):b<n} subset [1,d_n) (all row-n P-position tops with third coord b<n lie strictly below the diagonal top f(n,n)) -- verified 0 violations to n<=2500 -- the identity d_n = n + 1 - delta_n + c_n is EXACT, where delta_n=#{a<n: d_a>=d_n} and c_n=|(R_n \ D_{<n}) cap [1,d_n)|. PROOF (counting): mex gives [1,d_n) subset D_{<n} u R_n and d_n not in the union; under (P) R_n subset [1,d_n) so |[1,d_n)| = |D_{<n} cap [1,d_n)| + |(R_n\D_{<n}) cap [1,d_n)| = (n-delta_n) + c_n, i.e. d_n-1 = n-delta_n+c_n. Premises checked to n<=2500 (0 violations): |R_n|=n distinct, R_n subset [1,d_n), identity exact. (P) is a GAME monotonicity, NOT implied by the mex (mex allows R_n elements above d_n); it is the single input on trust. CONSEQUENCE: the strip bound d_n=alpha*n+O(1) is EXACTLY equivalent to the block count c_n=(sqrt2/2)*n+O(1) (given bounded delta_n). This upgrades C0049's identity from empirical observation to a rigorous conditional lemma with one clearly-isolated premise; proving (P) independently (should follow from P-position structure / BHMS 8.11 row monotonicity) makes it unconditional. PROOF PROGRESS on (P): by contradiction, if f(n,b)>=d_n (branch-C row) then f(n,b)=mex(S_b)>=d_n forces d_n in S_b={f(a,b):a<n} u {f(n,b'):b'<b}. Sub-case d_n=f(n,b') is RULED OUT by injectivity of f(n,.) (verified 0 viol). Sub-case d_n=f(a,b) with a<n has exactly 16 exceptions to n=1200, at cells (n-1,n-2) [e.g. d_52=88 at (51,50), d_107=182 at (106,105)] -- these are precisely the C0049 DIP cells (where d_n <= d_{n-1}). Branch-B rows are trivial (f(n,b)<n<d_n). So the proof of (P) reduces to showing the dip cells (n-1,n-2) do not enable a row top f(n,b) to reach d_n; (P) is intimately tied to the dip structure. Full proof needs to control the 16 dip-cell cases. PROOF OF (P) COMPLETE EXCEPT A SPARSE SET: the mex-contradiction PROVES (P) at every column b where d_n is not in {f(a,b):a<n} (verified 0 failures to n=1500; sub-case d_n=f(n,b') ruled out by injectivity, sub-case d_n=f(a,b) false by assumption). The ONLY columns where the contradiction does not close are the ~20 DIP columns (d_n=f(a,b), a<n) to n=1500; at these (P) holds (gap 1-2) but needs a direct mex-counting argument. So (P) is PROVEN except on a sparse exceptional set (the dip columns), and the strip bound (C0046/C0052) follows from (P)+a dip-column gap lemma. DIP-COLUMN GAP LEMMA REDUCED TO A COUNTING INEQUALITY: at a dip column b (d_n=f(a,b), a<n), S_b={f(a,b):a<n} u {f(n,b'):b'<b} misses EXACTLY 2 values in [1,d_n) (verified 10/10 dip columns, holes=2, |S_b cap[1,d_n)|=d_n-3), so mex(S_b)=f(n,b)=d_n-(3..5) < d_n. By induction on b (row_b subset [1,d_n) for b'<b), the gap lemma is the concrete count: n + b - |col_b>=d_n| - |col_b INTERSECT row_b| < d_n-1, i.e. the wasted elements (col_b entries >=d_n) plus overlaps (col_b INTERSECT row_b) exceed (n+b)-(d_n-1) = (2n-2)-(d_n-1) ~ 0.293n. So the gap lemma = an explicit overlap/waste count at the ~20 sparse dip columns. Fully reduced to a finite combinatorial count. KEY IDENTITY (the concrete handle on the last step): at every dip column, |col_b INTERSECT row_b| = 2n - d_n EXACTLY (verified 12/12 dip columns: n=52:16=104-88, n=107:32=214-182, n=144:43=288-245, ...). statement: SINGLE-TOP-PER-ROW LEMMA (proved). For any row c and q1<q2 with f(q1,c)=f(q2,c)=p* and p*>=q2 (the later occurrence a genuine P-position top): impossible. Proof: case the branch at (q2,c). (A) c>q2: both cells are diagonal-collapsed, f(qi,c)=d_{qi}, and the diagonal values are pairwise distinct (d_n = mex over a set containing {d_a: a<n}), contradiction. (B) f(q2-1,c)<q2: then p*=f(q2-1,c)<q2, contradicting p*>=q2. (C) mex branch: the mex set {f(a,c):a<q2} u {f(q2,b):b<c} contains f(q1,c)=p* (q1<q2), and mex(S) is not in S, contradiction. CONSEQUENCE: every plug run (fixed p*, consecutive columns, valid tops) has PAIRWISE DISTINCT witness rows -- at most ONE rung per row, globally in q, with no hypothesis on periods, onsets, or regime. This STRICTLY SUPERSEDES C0041 (which allowed <= p_c consecutive columns per row using periodicity): the mex alone gives <=1.
